checks.why: an explicit implementation of a GENERIC interface method (`IOptions<T, P> IOptions<T, P>.Then`) answers for a call through the interface: the name is written with its type arguments
an explicit implementation of a generic interface PROPERTY answers for a read through the interface
an explicit property of a non-generic interface likewise
an implicit implementation's getter and setter are reached by a read and a write through the interface
an interface indexer dispatches to the implementing indexer
the private helper the accessors call is reached from every caller through the interface
an abstract property read on the base reaches each override, one of a set
a virtual property read on the base reaches the override
control: a read on the derived type is not a read of the sibling's override
the interface property itself keeps the reader the site is written against
the abstract declaration keeps its reader too
control: a non-virtual property on a class is unchanged -- nothing reads it
